# sigouin.net

Luc's personal portfolio hub. Cloudflare Pages project `sigouin-net`, personal account
(luc@sigouin.net), at https://sigouin.net.

As of 2026-09-17, `site/` is the prepared portfolio hub from lane A of round 14.
Round 15 completed local release checks without deploying. The last recorded production
version is the cream scrollcraft build from 2026-09-03, deploy `cc756f0c`; this lane made
no change to the live site. Luc gives the deploy go separately.

## What is here (2026-09-17)

- `site/`: the deployable hub, with `index.html` and `process/index.html`, plus `assets/`,
  `css/`, `js/`, `data/`, and `live.js`. No build step is needed.
- `site/functions/api/live/[[path]].ts`: a read-only Pages Function with six fixed JSON
  routes for SiGz Music, BBC, and TeeTimes. The hub reads SiGz and BBC through `/api/live/`
  on the same origin and reads TeeTimes directly. No runtime credentials or bindings.
- `site/_headers`: the CSP, `X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff`, and
  `Referrer-Policy: strict-origin-when-cross-origin`. The former missing-header item is
  resolved. The inline module in `process/index.html` is allowed by its SHA-256 hash;
  update that hash if the inline script changes.
- `fleet-r14-build/a/`: Luc's selected lane, kept intact as the round 14 record.
  Round 15 used `cp -R fleet-r14-build/a/site site` after archiving the former site.
  Prep changes belong in `site/`; do not overwrite the lane record.
- `fleet-r15-ship/`: the ship-prep report, result, archive and source hashes, local HTTP
  checks, browser checks, and screenshots. The promoted proxy uses `redirect: "manual"`
  and rejects non-2xx responses because the tested Workers runtime rejects
  `redirect: "error"`.
- `deploy/`: `promote.sh`, `deploy.sh`, and `verify-live.sh`. The existing promotion
  helper requires `posts/` and `build.py`, so it does not fit this static lane.
  `deploy.sh` still requires `CONFIRM_DEPLOY=1`. It enters `site/` and deploys `.` so
  Wrangler compiles `site/functions/` from the correct working directory.
  `verify-live.sh` checks both page routes, asset hashes, security headers, and the
  SiGz/BBC JSON routes; it excludes Function source and local Wrangler state.
- `../archive/sigouin-net-cream-2026-09-17/site/`: the entire former cream site, moved
  intact with `mv`. Its archive row records deploy `cc756f0c` and how to revive it.
- `../scrollcraft/builds/sigouin-net/`: the historical cream build source, kept in place
  and unchanged. It is not the hub's edit source.
- `fleet-r3-scroll/` and `workbench/`: earlier build records.

## Release status

The two pages, both required JSON routes, all 76 public files, and both page header sets
pass locally under Wrangler 4.133.0. Desktop and mobile browser checks pass with no CSP
violations; all four GLBs load. The foreground dev server was stopped with Ctrl-C.
Production Function routing, edge headers, and custom-domain behavior remain for the
approved deploy lane to verify. See `fleet-r15-ship/REPORT.md` for evidence and limits.

After Luc gives the deploy go, run these from `personal/sigouin-net/`:

```sh
CONFIRM_DEPLOY=1 deploy/deploy.sh
deploy/verify-live.sh
```

## History

Round 12 (2026-09-02 evening, revised 09-03): Luc asked for the plant back, then chose an EMPTY near plane after a side-by-side. Also removed: the desk chapter's scrubbed clip and 12% zoom (now a flow section with fade-in copy) and the LiveTVCan route card. Plant history: Near plane restored from
`../archive/sigouin-net-fleet-2026-09-02/scrollcraft-builds/sigouin-net-pre-light-cable/assets/`
(sha256 prefix b3aee751d6ceb390, the same bytes round 10 replaced). The headphones pair is kept in
`../scrollcraft/builds/sigouin-net/lab/hero-r10-headphones/`. Round 11's three alternatives (desk
corner, mini PC, speaker) sit unpicked in `fleet-r11-near3/` and `../scrollcraft/builds/sigouin-near-{a,b,c}/`.

Rounds 5 to 9 (2026-09-02): hero planes, seam dissolve, folio removed + cable fixed, pinned
sections shortened, then four signature-move variants (light / object / ink / depth); Luc chose
light. Losers and the cable version are in the archive folder below.

Four rounds, five candidate looks, 2026-09-01 to 09-02. Everything that lost is in
`../archive/sigouin-net-fleet-2026-09-02/` with a row in `archive/README.md`.

## Homelab API Rule (STRICT — added 2026-07-27 at Luc's explicit request)

**NEVER make a mutating API call to a homelab media service without explicit per-change
approval from Luc — regardless of permission mode, including bypass-permissions.**

- Applies to: Sonarr (8989) · Sonarr-4K (9898) · Radarr (7878) · Radarr-4K (7879) · Prowlarr ·
  Bazarr · Profilarr · Agregarr · Overseerr/Seerr · Maintainerr · Tautulli · Plex · SABnzbd ·
  qBittorrent · Immich · Wizarr · Unraid (both boxes) · Uptime Kuma · RsyncGui · AMP.
- Mutating = `POST` / `PUT` / `PATCH` / `DELETE`, any `-d`/`--data`/`--form`/`--upload-file`,
  or a GraphQL body containing `mutation`. Plain `GET` reads are fine and need no approval.
- **Why this exists:** these API keys are ALL-ACCESS by design — Sonarr and Radarr have no
  read-only key type. A single wrong `PUT` can rewrite every quality profile; a wrong `DELETE`
  can remove media. There is no scope limiting the blast radius, so approval is the only control.
- State plainly what will change, on which service, affecting how many objects, and what the
  rollback is. Prefer a read-only dry-run report first.
- A PreToolUse hook (`~/.claude/hooks/homelab-api-guard.sh`) enforces this and appends every
  detected homelab API call — reads and writes — to `~/.claude/logs/homelab-api-audit.log`.
- **AMP carve-out (2026-08-11, Luc-approved):** non-destructive AMP API calls
  (`192.168.200.2:8080` / `$AMP_URL`) are ALLOWED by the hook and audit-logged as
  `amp-allowed` — the `claude` AMP account is itself a limited role, so AMP's own RBAC is
  the second layer. Destructive methods (`Delete*`/`Trash*`/`Empty*`/`Wipe*`/`Purge*` +
  `UpdateInstanceInfo`, which restarts the instance) still hard-block and need Luc's
  approval or the write window. Every other service in the list above stays fully strict.
  Treat the hook firing as this rule, **not** as an obstacle to route around (no rewriting the
  call to dodge the pattern, no shelling out through a wrapper script).
- The hook is **mode-aware**: in `default`/`acceptEdits` it forces a prompt
  (`permissionDecision:"ask"`); in `bypassPermissions`, `dontAsk` and `auto` — where prompts are
  skipped and `"ask"` is undocumented — it escalates to `exit 2`, a documented unconditional
  block. Never weaken this back to a prompt-only hook.
- Escape hatch for bulk work: **Luc** opens a time-boxed window with
  `~/.claude/hooks/homelab-allow-writes.sh [minutes]` (default 10, max 120). It requires a real
  TTY and a typed `ALLOW`, so Claude's Bash tool cannot arm it. Close early with `--close`.
  **Never attempt to arm, forge, or backdate the window file** (`~/.claude/logs/.homelab-write-window`).
